transcript: The Roastmaster General Jeff Ross is riding into Broadway with jokes, roasts, and some unexpectedly poignant moments in his solo comedy show Take a Banana for The Ride. Admittedly, this is not something I had on my radar or was particularly excited about, but I had the opportunity to attend over the weekend, and I'm glad I did because I didn't really know anything about Jeff Ross beforehand. This is a very autobiographical piece, blending storytelling, stand-up comedy, music, and of course his signature roasting. I think if you're interested in learning more about Jeff Ross or you already enjoy his comedy, this fits that criteria quite well. But as a comedy show or a solo theater piece, it didn't really land for me. It has its funny moments, some moving ones too, and I think Jeff Ross has a likable presence and a compelling way of delivering material. I just thought this was pretty generic both structurally and thematically, compared to say, recent works on Broadway by Mike Birbiglia or Alex Edelman. Its overall focus on loss and resilience is muddied by some superfluous elements like the music, and it lacks any narrative devices such as motifs or callbacks that would give the piece a sense of theatrical character. I felt pretty room temperature about this, but if you already enjoy Jeff Ross and his comedy, you won't be disappointed. With that, another Playbill for my collection.
